title: Leveraging Transferable Knowledge Concept Graph Embedding for Cold-Start Cognitive Diagnosis
authors: Gao, W.; Wang, H.; Liu, Q.; Wang, F.; Lin, X.; Yue, L.; Zhang, Z.; Lv, R.; Wang, S.
venue: Proceedings of the 46th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR '23)
tldr: Proposes TechCD, a two-stage framework using knowledge concept graphs with GCN for domain-level zero-shot cognitive diagnosis where target domain has no student-exercise interactions.
problem_and_motivation: Cognitive diagnosis models require student-exercise interaction data, but new domains (e.g., new courses) lack such records. Existing cold-start methods using exercise text fail due to linguistic bias and overfitting.
approach: Proposes TechCD framework with two stages: Knowledge Concept Graph Embedding (KCGE) using GCN, and Domain Adaptive Diagnosis (DAD).
Uses pedagogical knowledge concept graph (KCG) as mediator connecting source and target domains across different courses/subjects.
Employs bottom-layer discarding in GCN to extract transferable student cognitive states while maintaining domain-specific exercise traits.
Implements three diagnostic functions within the framework: IRT, MIRT, and NeuralCD.
Evaluated on four real-world datasets (Core Math, Advanced Math, Junyi, ASSISTments) with cross-domain zero-shot prediction.
findings: num: TechCD outperforms all baseline models including NLP-based and GCN-based methods on zero-shot student performance prediction.
num: Best performance achieved by discarding only bottom-layer student embeddings (DS), not exercise embeddings (DE).
num: Out-domain datasets from other platforms improve TechCD prediction performance under limited access scenarios.
KCG enables exercise recommendation in cold-start target domains where traditional CDMs cannot operate.
TechCD generates reasonable diagnostic reports for concepts in both source and target domains.
Exercise recommendations balance smoothness (difficulty progression) and engagement (appropriate challenge level).

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Introduces the domain-level zero-shot cognitive diagnosis (DZCD) task as a formal problem. Proposes a transferable framework using knowledge concept graphs as mediators between domains, enabling cognitive diagnosis without target domain interaction data. Demonstrates that bottom-layer discarding in GCNs produces domain-transferable student embeddings while preserving domain-specific exercise traits.
directly_justifies: KCG enables cross-domain student cognitive state propagation without target interactions.
Bottom-layer discarding in GCN extracts transferable student embeddings.
TechCD outperforms NLP-based and GCN-based zero-shot methods.
limits: Focused on educational domain, not financial systems.
Requires a pre-existing knowledge concept graph linking domains.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematically scanned all topic domains (1.A-14.C). Assigned 5.B high relevance for direct address of cold-start profiling. Assigned 6.A and 7.E medium for predictive modeling and onboarding transferability. Assigned 6.B low for algorithmic overlap. Rejected topics 1.A-4.C, 8.A-14.C as the paper focuses on educational cognitive diagnosis rather than personal finance.

limitations: Requires pre-existing KCG connecting domains, which may not exist for all subject areas.
Evaluated only on mathematical domains; generalizability to other subjects unconfirmed.
KCG construction relies on expert-labeled relations which may introduce bias.
remember_this: Knowledge concept graphs enable zero-shot cognitive diagnosis across domains.
Bottom-layer GCN discarding produces transferable student state embeddings.
TechCD framework generalizes across IRT, MIRT, and NeuralCD diagnostic functions.
Exercise recommendations generated for cold-start domains where traditional models fail.
